index.title: The Key the Next Token Matches
index.prompt: After predicting "on", the model runs again on "the cat sat on". The new token "on" has the embedding (−1, −1, 0, 1) and sits at position 3, and head 1 of this model copies dimensions 3 and 4 of a token's vector into its query and dimensions 2 and 3 into its key. The head 1 keys of the first three tokens are (1.000, 0.000) for "the", (1.540, 1.010) for "cat" and (−0.416, 1.020) for "sat". In head 1, the query of "on" is compared with the keys of all four tokens, its own included. Which key gives the largest dot product?
index.answer: The key of "cat". Position 3 adds (sin 3, cos 3, sin 0.03, cos 0.03) = (0.14112, −0.98999, 0.03000, 0.99955), so the vector of "on" is (−0.85888, −1.98999, 0.03000, 1.99955). Head 1's query copies dimensions 3 and 4, (0.03000, 1.99955), and its key copies dimensions 2 and 3, (−1.98999, 0.03000). The dot products are 0.030 with "the", 0.03000 × 1.540 + 1.99955 × 1.010 = 2.066 with "cat", 0.03000 × (−0.416) + 1.99955 × 1.020 = 2.027 with "sat", and 0.0003 with itself. The key of "cat" wins by only about 0.04: the second number of the query is large, and the second numbers of the keys of "cat" and "sat" are almost equal.

theory.title: The Key the Next Token Matches

prompt.p: After predicting "on", the model runs again on "the cat sat on". The new token "on" has the embedding (−1, −1, 0, 1) and sits at position 3, and head 1 of this model copies dimensions 3 and 4 of a token's vector into its query and dimensions 2 and 3 into its key. The head 1 keys of the first three tokens are (1.000, 0.000) for "the", (1.540, 1.010) for "cat" and (−0.416, 1.020) for "sat". In head 1, the query of "on" is compared with the keys of all four tokens, its own included. Which key gives the largest dot product?

choices.explain: This is what the query would be without the position. The embedding of "on" alone has 0 and 1 in dimensions 3 and 4, so its head 1 query would be (0, 1), and the dot products with the keys of "cat" and "sat" would be 1.010 and 1.020. At position 3 the slow pair adds sin 0.03 = 0.030 to dimension 3, and that 0.030 times the first numbers of the keys, 1.540 for "cat" and −0.416 for "sat", tips the result the other way.

Position 3 adds (sin 3, cos 3, sin 0.03, cos 0.03) = (0.14112, −0.98999, 0.03000, 0.99955), so the vector of "on" is (−0.85888, −1.98999, 0.03000, 1.99955). Head 1's query copies dimensions 3 and 4, (0.03000, 1.99955), and its key copies dimensions 2 and 3, (−1.98999, 0.03000). The dot products are 0.030 with "the", 0.03000 × 1.540 + 1.99955 × 1.010 = 2.066 with "cat", 0.03000 × (−0.416) + 1.99955 × 1.020 = 2.027 with "sat", and 0.0003 with itself. The key of "cat" wins by only about 0.04: the second number of the query is large, and the second numbers of the keys of "cat" and "sat" are almost equal.

A token tends to match itself when its query and key are made with the same weights, as in head 2, where the query and key of "on" are both (−1.990, 2.000) and its own dot product, 7.96, is by far the largest. Head 1's query copies dimensions 3 and 4 but its key copies dimensions 2 and 3, so the query of "on", (0.030, 2.000), against its own key, (−1.990, 0.030), gives only 0.0003.
